source.title: Neurons Speak in Ranges: Breaking Free from Discrete Neuronal Attribution
source.authors: Muhammad Umair Haider; Hammad Rizwan; Hassan Sajjad; Peizhong Ju; A. Siddique

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests concept erasure on pretrained SAE features and reports that they are not strictly monosemantic, qualifying the claim that SAE features are canonical units. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports neuron overlap and concept-conditioned activation distributions, but these do not test the claim versions about superposition geometry, capacity as a cause, or SAE feature recovery. The reported SAE-feature intervention results in Table 32 are the results recorded here.
record.test_reason: Only the preliminary SAE experiment (Appendix N, Table 32) bears on a version. It probes V5 by masking concept-associated Gemma Scope features and measuring collateral damage to other concepts. That tests monosemanticity of selected features, a narrow slice of V5. The rest of the paper studies neuron-level activation ranges and its own masking method.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The SAE paraphrase is accurate, but the SAE section is a preliminary appendix. The main conclusion is that polysemantic neurons show concept-conditioned Gaussian-like activation ranges with limited overlap. Range-based masking (NeuronLens) erases target concepts about as well as neuron masking, with less auxiliary damage and smaller perplexity and MMLU costs.
record.recipe_differences: The original source studies toy-model superposition; this paper instead tests concept erasure with activation-range masking on pretrained SAE features in Gemma-2-2B.
record.method_sensitivity: The SAE results vary by SAE variant: the reported auxiliary-concept and perplexity changes differ between Width_16k / l0_285 and Width_65k / l0_197.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-30% salient GPT-2 neurons overlap heavily across classes, over 60% for two-class IMDB (Figure 2). Concept-conditioned activations of a neuron form Gaussian-like distributions with limited overlap: skewness near 0, kurtosis about 3-4, KS practical normality near 1 (Tables 1, 5, 7, 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Polysemantic LLM neurons encode different concepts in separable activation-magnitude ranges.

fits_no_version.finding: Full neuron masking of concept-salient neurons degrades auxiliary concepts and raises perplexity more than range masking does, across BERT, GPT-2 and Llama (Tables 3 and 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron-level polysemanticity causes collateral damage in concept-erasure interventions.

record.problems: The SAE experiment is described as preliminary and covers one model, one dataset, and two pretrained SAE variants. The results are aggregate values without uncertainty estimates or class-wise breakdown in Table 32.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, no sparsity or capacity sweeps, no geometry.
All of it: capacity as a cause is only cited.
All of it: alternative causes such as initialization (Lecomte et al.) are only cited.
Whether features are distributed across neurons, and whether SAEs recover sparse features. The neuron-overlap analysis uses coarse classes, not features.
Completeness, stability across runs, and canonicity. Only collateral effects of masking selected features are tested, on one model, one dataset and two SAEs.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' label is too strong. V5 as stated is about complete, stable, canonical units, and the study tests only collateral effects of masking frequency-selected features, without controls. The authors' 'not strictly monosemantic' is an interpretation of aggregate deltas. Rows r2 and r4 are the study's own method and should not carry V5 verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity and capacity sweeps, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity or important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.

The paper discusses other proposed causes of polysemanticity, including cited work, but does not test whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure or whether it is evidence of superposition.
The SAE experiment does not test whether SAE dictionaries recover sparse features from LLM representations or whether real-model features are distributed across many neurons.

The paper tests whether SAE features are strictly monosemantic in a concept-erasure setting, but does not test their stability across training runs or whether they are complete or canonical units in general.
The paper studies scalar neuron activation ranges, not whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B, Gemma Scope (Width_16k / l0_285)
rows.operation_detail: Full masking of selected SAE features for concept removal.

conditions.value: top 20% highest-activating features among features activating for at least 10% of the training set for a concept

rows.measure: Changes in target accuracy/confidence, auxiliary accuracy/confidence, and perplexity, as reported in Table 32.
rows.baseline: Unmodified model; Table 32 reports changes from baseline, not absolute baseline values.
rows.note: The auxiliary-concept accuracy and confidence drops indicate collateral effects from full feature masking; the authors conclude SAE features are not strictly monosemantic. Table 32 reports aggregate values without class-wise breakdown.
rows.check: Bears on V5 only as feature cleanliness. Masking about 81 selected 16k features drops target accuracy by 0.323 and auxiliary accuracy by 0.169. Some auxiliary damage may come from the selection rule (top 20% of frequently active features, likely including generic ones). There is no random-feature control.

relationships.condition: Gemma-2-2B with Gemma Scope 16k/l0_285 and 65k/l0_197 SAEs, DBPedia concept erasure
relationships.reason: Masking concept-selected SAE features also cuts auxiliary-concept accuracy by about 0.17 (r1, r3), so the selected features are not clean concept units. There is no random-feature control and the selection rule may admit generic features, so this qualifies rather than refutes V5.
relationships.display_finding: Masking the selected features also cut auxiliary-concept accuracy by about 0.17, though there was no random-feature control and the selection rule may admit generic features.

source_check.reason: Full feature masking reduces auxiliary accuracy by 0.169 and 0.175 alongside target reductions of 0.323 and 0.392 (r1, r3). The selection procedure and absence of a random-feature control limit the inference; completeness, stability and canonicality are untested.

reader_labels.condition: The two tested Gemma Scope SAE variants on DBPedia
reader_labels.reason: Both variants show auxiliary-concept effects under full feature masking, and the authors state SAE features are not strictly monosemantic (r1, r3); range masking reduces but does not eliminate collateral effects (r2, r4).
